evidence: app/package.json:10 — vite ^8.3.5 and typescript ^7.0.2, both current stable
app/package.json:8 — build is 'vite build' only; official vanilla-ts template uses 'tsc && vite build', so type errors never run in CI
app/src/vite-env.d.ts:1 — proper vite/client reference; main.ts:74-92 hand-rolled router is the normal no-framework pattern
app/src/api.ts:1-5 — runtime-injected window.__API_BASE_URL__ with import.meta.env fallback is a sensible Vite-config approach
idiomatic.rationale: Recognisably idiomatic vanilla-TS-on-Vite with current versions; the only real deviation is skipping type-checking in the build, which lets the two `any`s slip through.

evidence: app/src/main.ts:64-70 — every API failure (500, network) renders the Not found page, masking real errors
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:141-146 — per-move fetch failures are swallowed (catch → null) and rows silently dropped
app/src/main.ts:26-30 and app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:381-394 — proper stale-render/stale-request guards; no leaked listeners (element listeners die with innerHTML)
app/src/pages/home.ts:119-121 — page clamped in update() but URL keeps a stale ?page=; also an invalid ?type= value is silently ignored (home.ts:72-73)
app/src/components.ts:49 — inline onerror handler (CSP-hostile) rather than an event listener
correctness_risks.rationale: No serious bugs: race handling and HTML escaping are consistently right. The remaining risks are error-masking (everything 404s) and silent data loss on partial fetch failure.

evidence: app/src/api.ts:153-169 — single shared promise cache keyed by URL, unbounded but data-fixed and self-healing on failure
app/src/api.ts:184-215 — view formatters (humanize, formatDex, displayNumber) live in the data module
app/src/api.ts:330-390 — getHomeData builds an entire page view model inside the data layer
app/src/components.ts:5-13 — small focused HTML helpers with a single escapeHtml entry point, used everywhere
global_abstractions.rationale: Boundaries are mostly clean (data layer / HTML helpers / pages), but api.ts mixes transport, domain types, formatters and view-model aggregation and will need splitting if it grows further.

evidence: app/src/pages/home.ts:53-126 — short, linear, well-named functions; consistent template style across all pages
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:246-251 — spec-derived magic values (id > 10000) and METHOD_ORDER with zero explanatory comments; 1 comment line in the whole app
app/src/pages/details.ts:130-136 — RELATION_TERMS table is a nice data-driven touch
readability.rationale: A new teammate finds their way quickly; the only gap is that spec-derived rules (alternate-form exclusion, method ordering) are unexplained, and pokemon.ts at ~420 lines is the file that would benefit from comments most and has none.

evidence: app/package.json:8 — one-line fix: add tsc to the build script
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:144,150 — replace apiFetch<any> with the existing MoveRecord interface
app/src/main.ts:64-70 — separate an error state from the not-found page
review_cost.rationale: I'd approve after a round of small changes: add type-checking to the build, type the move fetches, and split real errors from 404s. Nothing structural needs rework.

findings.issue: Build script runs 'vite build' without 'tsc', so the strict-mode type checks are never enforced in CI; the official create-vite vanilla-ts template builds with 'tsc && vite build'.
findings.suggestion: Change to "build": "tsc && vite build" (or add a separate check script) so the strict tsconfig actually gates merges.

findings.issue: All non-NotFoundError failures (API 500s, network errors) render the Not found page, hiding real failures from users and from on-call debugging.
findings.suggestion: Add a distinct error state ('Something went wrong') and keep the 404 page for NotFoundError only.

findings.issue: Move metadata fetched with apiFetch<any> and typed as any in a strict-mode codebase; per-move fetch failures are swallowed and rows silently dropped from the moves tables.
findings.suggestion: Type as MoveRecord (already defined in api.ts) and surface failures instead of dropping rows.

findings.issue: api.ts has become a god module: transport + cache, domain types, view formatters (humanize, formatDex, displayNumber) and page-level view-model aggregation (getHomeData) in one file.
findings.suggestion: Split into api/client.ts (fetch+cache), api/types.ts, and shared/format.ts; keep aggregate loaders in their own module.

findings.issue: Inline onerror attribute on card sprites breaks under a CSP without 'unsafe-inline' and mixes behaviour into an HTML template.
findings.suggestion: Delegate error handling via a document-level listener or a data attribute handled by the card list renderer.

findings.issue: Hash-scroll logic duplicated: the router scrolls to the hash after rendering, and renderPokemonPage re-implements the same rAF scroll (pokemon.ts:413-418).
findings.suggestion: Keep the scroll in one place — the router — and delete the page-local copy.

findings.issue: update() clamps state.page to totalPages but the URL keeps the stale ?page= value, so URL and view disagree (e.g. /?page=999).
findings.suggestion: After clamping, replaceState with buildUrl(state) so the URL matches the rendered page.

findings.issue: Loading a Pokémon page fires up to ~100 parallel move/version-group fetches on first visit (bounded by data, deduped by cache, but a burst).
findings.suggestion: Acceptable for this fixed local API; if the API ever grows, batch or lazily fetch move details per visible table.

findings.issue: Spec-derived magic values (id > 10000 alternate-form exclusion, METHOD_ORDER, stat label map) carry no comments explaining where they come from; the whole app has one comment.
findings.suggestion: Add one-line comments citing the spec rule for the 10000 cutoff, method ordering and stat labels.

summary: A small, well-organised vanilla-TS-on-Vite app with current dependencies, disciplined HTML escaping and genuinely good stale-render race guards; I'd approve it after one round of small changes. The must-fix items are adding tsc to the build (type errors are currently invisible, and there are any-typed move fetches to prove it) and separating real API errors from the not-found page. Longer term, api.ts should be split before it becomes a god module, but nothing structural blocks the merge.
